Corrected: καθώς keeps a bare as. An answering καί stands and the ASV writes no correlative so, which is the configuration rule 82 names at 2CO.11.12 (καθὼς καὶ ἡμεῖς -> even as we) and EPH.2.3 (ὡς καὶ οἱ λοιποί -> even as the rest), where the bare even answers to the particle. The chapter's 2:4, where no καί stands, keeps even as whole on καθώς, and that difference is licensed by the source.

Corrected from unrepresented: rule 65's English-side test aligns an intensifying καί wherever the ASV writes a word for it, and here it writes even. Rule 82's closing clause is what places that word here rather than on the comparative, the bare-even gloss carrying where no correlative so competes.
Rule 62: the elliptical clause's predicate is a prepositional phrase, so the preposition carries the supplied verb did, headed on the prepositional word.

review_notes: Only s028 and s029 change: even (t029) moves from καθώς to the answering καί, leaving καθώς a bare as (t030). Every other unit, head and note is as the verse pass returned it.

The competing reading, even as whole on καθώς with the καί unrepresented, is what the verse pass took. It is refused because rule 82 cites 2CO.11.12 and EPH.2.3 by name as the units where a bare even with no correlative so answers to the particle, and 2CO.11.12's καθὼς καὶ ἡμεῖς is this same construction.

The supplied did in the comparative clause stays on ὑπό under rule 62 rather than on αὐτοί: a prepositional phrase stands as the clause's predicate, so rule 56's subject-carrier case does not apply. Reading it as a helper on the subject pronoun remains defensible.
τὰ αὐτά is unchanged and read under rule 102, the article taking the … things and the adjective taking same.
All 33 source and all 35 target ids are partitioned exactly once.
